pr_comments: Synchronous reads should block, allowing other threads to run.  Best result will likely be in the 4-8 range, but cloud and live environments might yield very different numbers.  This could be pretty informative for future performance reference.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
Fine universe algorithms are incredibly slow.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->

review_comments: Beautiful! just out of curiosity, did you test using `> Environment.ProcessorCount`? Like `Environment.ProcessorCount * 1.5`, Maybe there is room for even more juice
I did not try but I can. I wouldn't expect that to help since all of these reads are synchronous -- if we were doing async reads I would think we could squeeze a little more out of it

@Martin-Molinero -- tried 1.5x and didn't notice and improvements (statistically insignificant delay was actually observed) -- hunch is that it's just extra overhead and the threads are simply competing each other
